notes:
I wasn't able to research Job 23 this time, so I have no verse notes to give you.

The research tools failed before I could read any pages. My first attempt to fetch eight sources together (Enduring Word; Ellicott, Gill, the Pulpit Commentary, Barnes and Wesley on biblehub.com; the NET Bible notes; Precept Austin) was stopped by a tool limit. The single Enduring Word fetch that followed came back in a form I couldn't read before I ran out of tool calls for this turn. I read nothing, and your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, so I haven't written any notes from memory.

If you ask again, I'll fetch the pages one or two at a time so I don't hit the limit. I'd go in this order:

1. **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word (Job 23), then Ellicott, Gill, the Pulpit Commentary and Barnes on biblehub.com, then Precept Austin.
2. **How the traditions compare:** Wesley's Explanatory Notes (Methodist); Spurgeon's sermons on Job 23:3 and 23:10 (Baptist); Matthew Henry, Calvin's sermons on Job and Ligonier or The Gospel Coalition articles on 23:10 (Reformed); Lutheran pages on lcms.org or 1517.org, if there are any. Verse 10 ("I will come forth as gold"), verses 11–12 (Job's claim to have stayed on God's path) and verses 13–14 (God's unchangeable decree) are the most likely places for real differences.
3. **Other views:** the NET Bible notes, which matter especially for verses 6, 7, 13 and 17, where the Hebrew is hard; Haydock or Church Fathers material on newadvent.org; and gotquestions.org, which may mention how verse 10 is used in popular teaching about suffering.

You could also send one batch at a time (for example, "verses 1–9 from Enduring Word and Ellicott") so each part finishes within the limits.
